title: Bit flags and bit manipulation via std::bitset
recap: A bit can represent one Boolean flag. std::bitset groups a fixed number of bits and provides named operations for querying and changing individual positions.
Bit positions are numbered from right to left starting at zero. test queries a position, set turns it on, reset turns it off, and flip inverts it; count reports how many bits are on.
objectives: Represent eight independent flags with std::bitset<8>.
Use set, reset, and flip to manipulate named bit positions.
Use test and count to inspect the resulting flags.
warnings: Bit position zero is the rightmost bit, not the leftmost bit.
std::bitset is optimized for convenient bit operations, not necessarily minimum object size.
Give positions meaningful names instead of scattering unexplained numeric indexes.
challenge: Start with read and share permissions enabled in an eight-bit permission set. Enable write, disable read, and flip admin from off to on using named positions and std::bitset member functions. Print the final bits, the read and write states, and the number of enabled permissions.
hints: Name the read, write, share, and admin positions with constexpr std::size_t values 0 through 3.
Call set(writePosition), reset(readPosition), and flip(adminPosition) on the same std::bitset.
Enable std::boolalpha before printing test results, and use count() for the final line.
